utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Judge Baird cannot be with us for the first session today, so we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis for the first session. But before we proceed, I was told by the Victims and Witness Section that the witness wanted to address the Chamber. Yes, Mr. Garic. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Well, first of all, when preparing to come here I was told I would be arriving yesterday, on the 1st. So I arrived about 9.00 p.m. last night, went to the hotel. I prepared briefly with the team, worked until half past 11.00 approximately. I couldn't sleep because it's been a long time since I last flew by plane. I live to the east of Sarajevo at an altitude of about 600 metres. I work on Jahorina at an altitude of 1.700 metres and here the altitude is 0 or even below 0. That has had an influence on me. So I don't know whether I will be able testify correctly and authentically, having prepared so briefly with the team. If my request could be met, perhaps I could testify next Monday, next week, on the first working day. That's what I was told would happen. All of this is new to me. It's all been done in a hurry and I'm afraid I won't be able to convey with precision all the events that took place almost two decades ago. I'm not sure I'll be able to testify authentically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just out of abundance of caution, could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I understand -- you used the word or at least the word "authentically" was the word that was translated. I think what you probably meant was that if you were to testify today the quality of your evidence wouldn't be as high as it would be if you were able to rest until Monday. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's quite right. I came to testify here with the intention to help to tell my story, to tell the Chamber about what I can remember with regard to the events that took place over 20 years. I wanted to testify to the best of my ability, which would be in the interest of the Tribunal, the Prosecution, the accused, et cetera. So I would suggest, if my request could be granted, that I be allowed to prepare with the team, to have a rest, and to continue, or rather, to testify on the first working day next week, which is what I was told would, in fact, take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, what did you mean by saying that you would prepare with the team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my conversation with regard to my testimony here was in July. I gave a statement on Jahorina about two months ago, and I still haven't read through the statement as I should have. I haven't been presented with everything. What I had a look at yesterday -- well, there were two or three details that I didn't quite agree with. I would like to correct that, so that's what I meant by saying that I would like to prepare with the team. If I may continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In around May of 2004 I gave a statement in Belgrade. As far as I can remember, a certain gentleman Jonathan Tait-Harris [phoen] was his name, if I remember it correct, I gave him an interview because I was in Belgrade for a few days. When we took leave of each other, I was told I would be provided with a copy of the statement, a recording, I was told I would be sent the CDs, but this was never done. So it wasn't quite serious, although this gentleman, I think he was British, he gave me his card. I called him on a number of occasions but I couldn't reach him. So I haven't had a look at those statements either. It's only last night that I had a couple of hours to have a look at the statement. I need a little time to prepare myself, to focus, to have a rest. I have told you the reason for which I suggested that I should start testifying next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to hear from the parties. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Well, we did everything we could to try to maximise the use of the Chamber's time, but I think in light of the witness's position it would really be better to proceed on Monday. For one thing, we could prepare a revised statement, we can save some time by not having to go through a statement that has been corrected, and I think it would be better for the witness and better for the Chamber if we were able to do this in an orderly fashion. We had hoped that we could work with him last night, and I thank Mr. Sladojevic for working until almost midnight with the witness, but it appears that the witness is not really ready to be giving his testimony today and we apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good morning. Well, I mean, obviously the welfare of the witness is paramount here. The one thing I would notice is that there may be some inconsistency between the witness's need to rest and his wish to prepare over the weekend with the Defence. And in that regard I would note that - I think as the Chamber is aware - we received a substantial number of corrections and additions to the statement yesterday evening. I think there were 17 paragraphs in all, including some substantive changes to the statement and significant new information on new topics. And we're in the Chamber's hands on this, but I would ask that if there is to be further proofing over the weekend that it would be limited to preparing a revised statement incorporating the corrections that we have already received and without provision of further new information so that we're not in the situation on Monday morning that we were in on this morning, being presented with substantial amount of new information and very little time to absorb it into our cross-examination preparations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, does the Defence need further proofing or new information from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that we need new information, but I think in any kind of contact with the witness if he were to provide us with new information we ought to communicate that to the Prosecution even though it might be something they would prefer not to receive. But -- so I don't think it would be appropriate to limit the proofing in any way, but we'll make every effort to have the statement, if we do take a revised statement, if we're given time, to have it limited to the corrections that are being made. But if he does provide us with new information we can't stop him and we can't ignore it, so I don't think there should be any limitations on the proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We could have started hearing his evidence but we are minded to postpone the proceedings in light of the well-being of the witness. So I was wondering whether there's no contact with the witness whatsoever, would it cause much problems on the part of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we were prepared to go forward this morning, so it wouldn't cause any problem, but it would be a lot better if we could prepare a statement so that when we came into court on Monday it took ten minutes instead of 45 minutes to get the evidence out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the -- any revision of the statement should have been -- should be disclosed to the Prosecution by the close of business time today. Would that be feasible?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Ms. Gustafson, is it acceptable to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Garic, we are going to postpone the proceedings until Monday, and please take a good rest and I hope you recover very soon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.47 a.m.,
